title: Console essentiality matrix and scope reduction plan for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Engineering and design constraints plus cost ceilings force a surgical cut of Console features for the initial observability beta. This ticket captures the essentiality matrix exercise we ran (PM/Eng/Design), the decisions on which dashboard cards, tracing flows, and cost breakdowns are landing in the alpha, and the implementation plan for graceful degradation. Goal: deliver a minimal, coherent surface that allows early adopters to diagnose latency and cost regressions while keeping delivery risk and infra cost within the Q2 delta budget.

Scope reductions proposed here focus on: 
- Dashboard card set: prioritize route-level latency + token cost per-route; remove per-token heatmaps and long-tail percentile breakdowns from alpha.
- Tracing: include sampled end-to-end request traces for P95/P99 failure investigations; omit full-span flamegraphs and synthetic trace generation.
- Cost breakdown: include route-level aggregated spend and top-5 model contributors; postpone per-customer lineage and allocation tagging until beta.

This ticket documents acceptance criteria, rollbacks/fallback behaviors, staging rollout plan, and sign-offs required (Eng infra, Runtime, Security). It also lists follow-ups for the re-add cycle (beta) and tracking signals we will capture to reevaluate cut decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Alpha dashboard includes 3 consolidated cards: global throughput, top-10 routes by 1h token consumption, and route median latency (1m resolution).
Tracing surface exposes sampled traces for any error-rate spike above configured threshold (default 0.5% over baseline) and links to the corresponding request id in logs.
Cost breakdown widget shows aggregated spend by route and top-5 model contributors with hoverable token/call totals; no per-customer or tag-based allocations in alpha.
All dashboard cards load with under 1.5s cold load and adhere to console-2025.04 styleguide; UX accepts degraded-mode message when backend telemetry is delayed >5s.
Rollout includes canary of 5% of orgs with opt-in feedback button that records structured feedback to the 'console-observability-alpha' feedback table.
If backend trace sampling pipeline is unavailable, tracing card shows a clear fallback state and a pointer to 'Trace service degraded' runbook with playbook link.
Telemetry metrics emitted: dashboard_card_render_latency, cost_widget_refresh_latency, trace_sampling_rate — all wired to the observability bucket for post-launch analysis.
decisions: Adopt essentiality matrix ranking (critical / useful / deferred) rather than feature-by-feature voting to avoid scope creep.
Defer per-customer cost allocation and fine-grained percentile dashboards to beta (post alpha).
Tracing: include sampled traces only; postpone span-level flamegraphs until after sampling and storage budget validated.
UX: Show degrade-to-minimal messaging (single CTA) rather than multi-option fallback to simplify implementation.
Rollout: opt-in canary at 5% with telemetry gating for ramping to 25% then 100% if no major regressions.
tasks: PM: finalize essentiality matrix and publish the prioritized cut list in Confluence (link below).
Design: provide simplified card comps (small, medium) and degraded-mode copy by 2025-03-17.
Eng Backend: implement condensed cost aggregation endpoint (route-level, top-5 models) and add fallback status flags by 2025-03-24.
Runtime: expose trace-sampled request id in the request metadata and wire to trace indexer (PR referenced below).
Frontend: implement three alpha cards and degraded-mode UI with acceptance tests and storybook stories.
comments: 2025-03-11 - Asha Patel: Ran cross-functional cut workshop. Outcome: unanimous support for prioritizing route-level signals. Action: Design to rapid-prototype three small cards.
2025-03-13 - Lucas Ng (Eng Infra): Flagged memory pressure concerns in the trace indexer if sampling stays >15%. Recommend default sampling 5% and allow org override.

2025-03-14 - Emily Chen (Design): Uploaded compact comps and copy for degraded mode. Designer note: reuse existing 'insights-empty' component to speed implementation. Link: https://confluence.redwood/console/compact-comps

2025-03-15 - Luca Moreno (Assignee): Implementation plan drafted. Backend endpoint POST /v1/internal/cost/summary returns route-level aggregates. Dev PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1278
2025-03-16 - Security review: Confirmed no sensitive customer tagging in alpha. Need to document retention policy for traces in runbook. Security contact: Priya Kapoor.
2025-03-18 - PM note: ETA holds. Design acceptance pending minor copy iteration. Plan to start canary on 2025-03-25 if infra tests pass.
followups: Beta re-eval checklist (scheduled 6 weeks after alpha): decide on reintroducing percentile cards and per-customer allocation.
Cost: perform month-1 cost delta analysis vs no-console baseline and present to finance and infra.
Feature: plan for 'allocation tags' spike with schema for tagging and sample export.
notes: Trade-offs: The alpha sacrifices granularity for faster delivery and predictable infra spend. Team agrees that core use-cases (route-level cost + latency) unlock >70% of initial diagnostic value.
Fallback UX: keep copy prescriptive (what happened + next steps) and include single 'Retry' action rather than multiple technical options.
Metrics gating: If dashboard_card_render_latency > 2s for 10% of requests in canary, block ramp and iterate.
